class_meanings.none: Very little modelled water erosion; not zero or a safe-loss guarantee
class_meanings.high: Published high or higher erosion bands combined

rules.rationale: Pete approved these four class definitions on 2026-11-25: Very little 0-1; Low >1-3; Medium >3-5; High >5 tonnes/ha/year. Retain published very-low, low and moderate bands; merge published high and higher bands. RuralScan uses upper-inclusive endpoints. The article applies European Soil Bureau bands globally; 5 starts its high class while 10 is its separate generic tolerable-erosion benchmark, neither a soil-specific safe-loss guarantee. Approval covers the class interpretation; the documentation-only binding and runtime release remain unapproved. See priority/research/2026-11-25-soil-erosion-global-classes.md for the approval quote and rationale.

rules.rationale: Pete approved the four classes and rationale on 2026-11-25: WRI Low -> Very little; Low-medium -> Low; Medium-high -> Medium; High and Extremely high -> High. Renaming and merging are RuralScan conventions, not a claim of absent scarcity. rules.rationale: Pete approved these four classes, rationale and coverage limits on 2026-11-25: IPC chronic area levels 1 Minimal -> Very little, 2 Mild -> Low, 3 Moderate -> Medium, 4 Severe -> High. Published chronic severity fits medium- and long-term rural investment scoping. Reuse an applicable published classification, not a new IPC assessment. Country coverage and validity differ; outside assessed coverage, missing, invalid and inapplicable records remain unknown. Acute IPC phases and FIES prevalence are not equivalent. Local dataset selection and runtime release remain outstanding. See priority/research/2026-11-25-food-insecurity-classes.md for approval quote and source rationale.

binding.field: 100 * (1 - actual_yield / attainable_yield); compatible crop fields and asset pending selection
binding.spatial_support: No spatial asset selected. Source demonstration uses country maize/rice/wheat averages; national figures cannot create within-country variation. Crop, water regime, management, units and period must match.

class_meanings.none: Very little: published limited crop yield gap; not zero gap
class_meanings.high: Published severe and very severe crop yield gaps combined

rules.rationale: Pete approved these four crop production gap classes and limitations on 2026-11-25: Very little 0-20%; Low >20-40%; Medium >40-60%; High >60-100% of attainable yield. FAO SOLAW 2025 Figure 19 supplies five bands; RuralScan relabels, merges the top two and uses upper-inclusive endpoints. Annex 1.2 uses high-input GAEZ v5 attainable yields and FAOSTAT country yields, distinct from the pixel yield-achievement product. Initial demonstration covers maize/rice/wheat, 2001-2020; other crops and spatial transfer require contextual review. Not livestock, pasture NPP or mixed-system classes. Missing observations or nonpositive attainable yields remain unknown; negative gaps retain raw values for review, not clipping. Non-cropped land is outside the measure. Gap is baseline need, not NbS-closable benefit. Dataset selection and runtime release remain outstanding. See priority/research/2026-11-25-production-gap-classes.md.
